text:
[RLOW.6.1.4] **The compiler must not simplify `and` / `or` by absorption or
distributivity.** Neither law holds once an operand can fault ([LNUL.4.2]):
`a and (a or b)` → `a` turns the fault `null and (null or t)` yields into
`null`, and distributing can do the same with an `EngineError`. The compiler may
reorder operands and apply commutativity, associativity, De Morgan and double
negation, which do hold. It may fold a literal `false` operand of an `and` (a
literal `true` of an `or`) to that literal, because the literal decides whatever
the other operands raise.

alloy.name: lnul_5_4__v5_false_decides
alloy.note: NARROWING: a false anywhere decides whatever the rest would raise, and nothing is recorded -- so folding a literal false operand is sound (RLOW.6.1.4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_5_4__false_decides
idris.note: NARROWING: a false guard decides the `where` wherever it stands, whatever any other conjunct -- the guarded tail included -- would raise, and nothing is recorded: [IRET.9.6]'s narrowed tail evaluated before its guard meets a `false` guard that absorbs its TypeError. And folding a literal `false` operand is sound (RLOW.6.1.4). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: rlow_6_1_4__absorption_fails
idris.note: ABSORPTION DOES NOT HOLD: `null and (null or t)` is the fault t, where the law would give null -- the clause's own example, so the compiler must not simplify by it.

idris.name: rlow_6_1_4__distributivity_fails
idris.note: DISTRIBUTIVITY DOES NOT HOLD: `null and (true or e)` is null, `(null and true) or (null and e)` is the EngineError e.
